headline: Former Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon has told New York Magazine that colleagues once showed him a Claude chatbot trained to 'solve' humor, and that he told them it had not.
score_reason: Pool 3 lowered 1: the headline presents as Anthropic's claim what is one former employee's memory of a Slack channel, relayed with a mocking tone.
importance_line: It gives readers a light, critical view of the culture at Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, but it rests on one former employee's undated recollection and the article carries no reply from Anthropic.
summary: Futurism reports, citing a New York Magazine interview, that Jacob Coxon, who left the AI company Anthropic after saying the AI industry was 'gambling with our lives', recalled a Slack channel with a version of its Claude chatbot trained to 'solve humor', where colleagues said they had solved it and he told them they had not. Futurism treats the story as a sign that AI builders can be out of touch; it rests on one person's memory and gives no reply from Anthropic.
notes: Read at Futurism, which relays a New York Magazine interview; the New York Magazine page itself was not read, so the link is the Futurism page. The Slack-channel anecdote is undated.
